limitations: No Digital Macaroni hands-on test was completed.
Most scored feedback comes from Product Hunt.
The current pricing page exposed plan features but not numeric paid prices in the research response.

sources.name: Motion Design community critique of Jitter output

claims.statement: Jitter imports editable Figma designs and provides templates, presets, a visual timeline, collaboration, and video, GIF, and Lottie exports.
The Free plan allows unlimited drafts, three workspace files, and 720p 30fps exports with a Jitter watermark.
Pro removes the watermark and adds unlimited files, 1080p 60fps, ProRes, and WebM. Max adds 4K 120fps, transparent export, and frame-by-frame export. Ultra mainly raises AI capacity.
Quick browser use, familiar design controls, Figma import, and presets are repeated strengths.
The software can make simple motion easier, but the quality of a finished marketing video still depends on design, timing, sound, and editing judgment.

scoreRationale.onboarding: The browser, free plan, templates, and familiar controls make the first animation approachable.
scoreRationale.product: Jitter is strong for text, logo, product-screen, and social animations, but it is not a complete replacement for deeper motion and video tools.
scoreRationale.support: Public evidence is too thin for a strong support judgment.
scoreRationale.billing: The free plan is useful for testing. Paid tiers are easy to compare by output need, but current numeric prices should be checked live.
scoreRationale.overall: Jitter is useful when a designer needs to make existing visual work move without learning a full professional animation package.

conflictsAndUnknowns: Product Hunt feedback is strongly positive, but evidence from other review platforms is thin.
A simple tool can speed production without giving a beginner good animation judgment.
No hands-on workflow or export test was completed.
